# 0328. Automatically generated interface dispatch tables

Date: 2026-10-03

## Status

Accepted. Supersedes the decision in
[ADR 0315](0315-bc2cpp-interface-tables-measured-not-built.md) to not build
interface tables; that census stays valid as the baseline this measures against.

## Context

bc2cpp repeats exact-class chains at many sites and already has a memoized
shared table for names above sixteen mandatory-argument candidates (ADR 0227).
ADR 0315 found that a table alone does not prove its fallback unreachable.
The request is to build automatically generated tables with reusable per-class
implementations while preserving those proof boundaries.

## Decision

Add opt-in `BC2CPP_INTERFACE_TABLES=1`. Before a blockless polymorphic chain,
build a table when five to sixty-four eligible exact classes answer the name.
Use the existing POLY_TABLE row lookup, eight-entry memo, owner-class cache,
and VM reset lifecycle. Share tables by method, arity and resolved row list.

Each cell points to a generated adapter with the uniform signature
`mrb_value(mrb_state*, mrb_value receiver, mrb_value args...)`. Adapters can call
compiled Ruby methods (including optional arguments), inherited implementations,
ivar accessors, audited Array/String natives with no argument guard, and RGSS
direct entries without integer coercion. Identical adapters share a function;
only adapters referenced by surviving tables are emitted. Native helper
selection includes adapter bodies.

Require a closed world, global refusal and singleton-freedom checks, stable
constant identity, stable visibility, and no installer of the method name.
Ruby cells reuse POLY candidate/inheritance eligibility and CALL_FACTS's
per-class native-free check; only public methods join. Native cells reuse their
existing audited eligibility checks. Integer native cells are excluded because
class equality cannot distinguish immediate Integers from bigints. Entries
requiring an argument guard or call frame remain outside the table.

A miss uses `guarded_fallback_line`, including visibility/arity checks and
NoMethodError proofs. This does not infer receiver classes from method spelling
or turn an unproven miss into an error. Block calls and short chains keep their
previous paths. Unset/zero mode preserves existing generated output.

The separate `claude/bc2cpp-native-class-arms-q4m` branch improves per-class
lookup and receiver-set proofs (ADR 0323). Those improvements can feed the
same fallback later; this change does not copy that branch's proof changes or
its FLOW_CORE_DIRECT optimization.

## Why this supersedes ADR 0315

0315 declined to build a table because its goal was *removing the else arm*,
and no table removes one: a miss still needs the by-name fallback the closed
world has not proved dead. The lever that removes an else arm is a stronger
receiver-set proof, and PR 1999 (ADR 0323) is that work. This change takes the
opposite bet — a table is worth building for the sites that are already
dispatching, because a shared table of per-class adapters is smaller source
and a flatter lookup than repeating the chain. 0315's own measurement (the
126 sites at the POLY_SMALL_N cap, plus the 5-8 and 9-13 bands) is what this
builds for, so the census is reused rather than rerun.

## Consequences

On master `fdf8a884`, same local source inputs, the shipped wio comparison
selects fifteen interface tables for 576 sites (554 RPG2k/Game, 11 LCF and
11 RGSS/other), with 82 surviving adapters. Including the existing update
table, sixteen tables ship. Generated C++ falls from 21,409,974 bytes / 440,968
lines to 20,818,687 bytes / 432,618 lines: 591,287 fewer bytes (2.76%). This is
source size, not a firmware flash measurement.

Body by-name sends remain 2,542; helper sends 24; block funcalls 400; body
funcalls 28; NoMethodError sites 4,380. No fallback removal is claimed.

An arm64 native `-O2` microbenchmark, eight trivial implementations, two
million direct `_impl` calls per sample, three samples, measured median CPU
nanoseconds per call:

| Receiver | Chain | Table |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First class | 6.37 | 8.29 |
| Last class | 39.04 | 7.35 |
| Rotating eight classes | 22.06 | 9.55 |

A one-site fixture costs more: generated bytes 27,368 to 30,009 and linked
executable bytes 748,216 to 749,384. Tables pay through sharing and receiver
mix; they are not universally faster. Keep the mode opt-in until target
benchmarks justify a default threshold. No game-throughput claim is made.

`scripts/bc2cpp_interface_tables_check.rb` compares interpreter results and
exceptions, repeated hits/misses, native calls and accessors, GC and two
compiled VMs. It checks open worlds, installers, visibility changes,
singleton makers, native overrides, rebinding, prepends and argument guards.
`scripts/bc2cpp_interface_tables_bench.rb` reproduces the timing comparison.
